Three of the five (7m27Go3K1d0, Bw58mV015z4, ZiEGOgTC56Y) also have no stored per-video summary and so are invisible to the router anyway — which is a coincidence of the corpus, not the exclusion working, and is why the other two are named here explicitly.

packs.name: Resume design
packs.blurb: What a technical resume has to do on the page before anyone reads it closely.
packs.routing_text: How should a software engineer or data scientist write their resume? Bullet points, professional summary, page length, formatting and layout, ATS keyword matching, quantified impact and metrics, tailoring a CV to one job description, and what a recruiter looks for in the seconds they spend skimming it.

packs.name: Job search
packs.blurb: Everything around the resume: profile, outreach, projects, interviews.
packs.routing_text: How do you actually get interviews and land a tech job? Optimising a LinkedIn profile, headline, about and featured sections, getting found by recruiters, networking and outreach messages, referrals, portfolio and project work, applying, preparing for interviews, mock interviews, behavioural and STAR answers.

packs.name: System design
packs.blurb: Distributed-systems decisions and the tradeoffs the speakers refuse to skip.
packs.routing_text: Designing large scale distributed systems: database sharding and partitioning, caching strategies and invalidation, replication, consistency and availability tradeoffs, transactions and isolation levels, distributed message queues, REST API design, latency, throughput and capacity estimation in a system design interview.

packs.name: App architecture
packs.blurb: How to cut an application into modules that survive contact with a team.
packs.routing_text: Structuring an application codebase: modular monoliths versus microservices, module and service boundaries, vertical slices, hexagonal ports and adapters, clean and onion architecture, domain driven design, coupling and cohesion, encapsulation, and keeping business logic out of the web framework.
